release_name: Near me: watchdog + iOS-specific Settings path
notes: Follow-up to v27.6.2. Two further fixes to the location-refused flow, both found by checking rather than assuming the previous fix was complete. (1) locationRequestInFlight was only ever reset inside the two browser callbacks; iOS home-screen web apps have a known history of never invoking either one for a blocked permission, which would leave it stuck true forever and make every later tap of Try again a genuine no-op - no re-render, nothing. Added an independent 9-second watchdog, plus a request-id guard so an abandoned requests late callback can never overwrite whatever a subsequent retry already produced. (2) The refusal message previously said only to open Settings and find this app or your browser - correct but vague. It now detects standalone (Home Screen installed) mode and gives the actual iOS path: Settings, scroll to the app (same name as its icon, since the manifest name is English-only and could not be asserted with confidence), tap Location, choose While Using the App; with the Privacy & Security -> Location Services route as a fallback if not listed. A plain browser tab still gets the original, more general wording. Verified: a hung request self-resolves after 9s with a real message instead of staying stuck; a genuinely stale late callback is correctly ignored once a newer request has taken over; both languages correctly switch to the Home Screen wording only when standalone mode is detected, and a plain browser tab keeps the original text.
